summary: 100-ft steel tower in Hampton County, SC (NHLR US 1005), built circa 1936, administered by the SC Forestry Commission and now housing radio repeaters.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a 10'x7'x7' steel cab; register says it appears to be a Bethlehem Steel model
facts.agency: South Carolina Forestry Commission (administrator named on the NHLR page)

events.note: Register says built circa 1936; builder not named
Registered March 27, 2014; nominated by Michael T. Finch, Jr.

evidence.supports: tower is in Hampton County and listed as US 1005, SC 28
100-foot steel tower with 10'x7'x7' steel cab, built circa 1936
evidence.quote: This 100-foot steel tower features a 10'x7'x7' steel cab and was built circa 1936.

evidence.supports: appears to be a Bethlehem Steel model
evidence.quote: It appears to be a Bethlehem Steel model.

evidence.supports: administered by South Carolina Forestry Commission
poor condition; used to house radio repeaters
evidence.quote: Currently in poor condition, it is currently used to house radio repeaters.

evidence.supports: alidade style differs from most other SC towers
evidence.quote: The tower has a different style of alidade than seen in most other South Carolina towers.

evidence.supports: nominated by Michael T. Finch, Jr.
first Forestry Commission fire tower erected August 1930 near Camden
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.

evidence.supports: Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: two towers took bearings on smoke with an alidade
evidence.quote: When a smoke was spotted, each of two towers would record its direction using a large compass table and a sighting device called an alidade.

evidence.supports: operator hours depended on the fire danger
evidence.quote: The tower operator’s hours in the tower cab depended on the fire danger.

evidence.supports: Commission built about 140 towers between mid-1930s and 1993 (Leesville entry)
evidence.quote: This is one of the original ~140 fire towers built by the South Carolina Forestry Commission between the mid-1930s and the abandonment of the system in 1993.

notes_for_editor: The NHLR detail page was read in full and gives the tower facts. The tie to the Forestry Commission rests on the NHLR administrator line; no source reads that Varnville was one of the Commission's lookouts in service, so the story treats it as likely, not certain. The 140-tower figure comes from the Leesville entry, not from this page. Date reading: 'built circa 1936' is the register's estimate. Height 100 ft converted to 30.5 m. Access unknown. The SCFC history page was not separately read (it did not add anything tower-specific). A WebSearch hit for an FCC tower registration at Varnville (2007) was not used because it is not shown to be this tower. No corrections proposed.
